settings.title: Explain how local delivery and placement work
settings.text: Let buyers know whether curbside, threshold, room-of-choice, or full installation is included for nearby orders.
settings.feature_list:
Delivery window communication
Stair or access requirements
Protection for floors and walls
Inspection at handoff
settings.callout_text: Parking access, stair details, elevator availability, and any delivery restrictions.

settings.title: Set expectations for crate shipping and freight appointments
settings.text: For oversized furniture and millwork, explain how freight is quoted, whether liftgate service is included, and when damage must be reported.
settings.feature_list:
Crated packaging for transit
Freight carrier scheduling
Liftgate or dock requirements
Damage reporting window on delivery
settings.callout_text: A short inspection checklist on this page helps prevent disputes after delivery.

settings.title: Estimate parcel cost and delivery time before you book the shipment
settings.text: Customers need to understand that handcrafted work often has two clocks: fabrication time and delivery time. The estimator below uses rough dimensions and weight so buyers can compare USPS, UPS, and FedEx before requesting a final quote.
settings.feature_list:
Build queue estimates
Transit windows after completion
Carrier comparison by size and weight
Storage policy for delayed receipt

settings.heading: Shipping information should answer practical questions before checkout
settings.intro: Use this page to explain delivery method, freight handling, timing, and rough parcel pricing before a customer reaches out.

settings.heading: Estimate shipping by carrier before requesting the final quote
settings.intro: Use the dimensions and approximate weight from a ready-made item description, or enter the measurements from your custom-order plan. Choose USPS, UPS, or FedEx to compare a rough shipping range and delivery window, then confirm the final numbers on the carrier site.
